results: Requirement N31 verified: scripts/package.sh packages the complete product including the compiled Go engine binary, web UI assets, offline Rego rules, reproducible source archive with build recipes, CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM, third-party notices, cryptographic checksums and provenance metadata.
A web-only artifact does not satisfy the complete release gate; the complete distribution in dist/release contains both engine and web runtimes, offline rules and reproducible source archive.

Staged-byte boundary atomicity: all files are assembled in an isolated staging directory dist/.staging-release-<pid> and atomically promoted to dist/release via directory rename upon passing internal SHA-256 verification.
Interrupted write resilience: killing the writer at the staging boundary or during build leaves the prior valid release intact and prevents partial bytes from leaking into authoritative state.
Replay and quota resilience: packaging is idempotent and handles disk-full/quota errors with clean cleanup traps and retryable abort.
Fail-closed security: checksum verification fails closed if any binary, rule, asset or manifest is tampered; reverse proxy template strips unauthenticated identity headers at ingress.
Zero network build recipe: policyhelix-source.tar.gz unpacks into a self-contained source tree buildable offline with standard Go 1.23+ and Node 24+ toolchains.
No database schema, migration, .env or Dockerfile was modified; all core features remain open-source Apache-2.0 with pinned upstream licenses.
observed_limitations: Artifacts were compiled and verified on Linux x86_64; cross-platform packaging for other architectures is planned for later release tasks.
